title: Prevent transient privilege window and audit loss during KMS envelope rotation by coordinating RBAC cache invalidation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A race condition between KMS envelope rotation and our RBAC cache invalidation path in private control planes can produce two critical issues: 1) missing audit events for token unwrap/authorization and 2) a short-lived privilege elevation window when a rewrapped credential is accepted by a stale RBAC mapping. Several customers (Acme Analytics, Finora Bank) reported suppressed audit logs and an unexplained permission spike during scheduled key rotations in private clusters.

Root cause hypothesis: During KMS envelope rotation we issue async rewrap/unwrap operations for customer envelopes. Concurrently, RBAC constraints are invalidated via the control plane cache invalidation signal. If the RBAC invalidation is delayed (by network jitter or a control-plane restart), older role bindings are still considered valid while tokens have been rewrapped against new envelope keys. Because audit plumbing uses the unwrap event as the authoritative source for the event, a timing mismatch leads to audit events being dropped and an edge case where a rewrapped credential maps to a higher-privilege role due to stale rolebinding index.

Reproduction steps (internal):
- Provision a private control plane with RBAC cache TTL set to 45s and enable envelope rotation every 1m.
- Initiate envelope rotation and simultaneously apply a rolebinding change (remove restrictive binding, add permissive binding).
- Observe unwrap events in the KMS proxy logs and check the control-plane audit sink for missing events and enforcement logs.

Immediate mitigation applied (customer-facing):
- Deployed a hotpatch to the private control plane that serializes envelope rotation completion and an explicit RBAC cache flush: rotation controller now waits for ack from rbac-indexer before marking rotation complete.
- Provisioned a temporary elevated monitoring dashboard and alert that detects unwrap-without-audit patterns and triggers an automated rollback of rolebinding changes for impacted tenants.

Planned durable fix:
1) Make envelope rotation transactional with RBAC index: rotation controller will emit a rotation-phase marker; RBAC indexer will process markers as ordered commits and only accept tokens that unwrap against the committed envelope version.
2) Harden audit pipeline to surface unwraps even if indexer lag exists (replayable audit events persisted in KMS-proxy until control-plane ack).
3) Add a control-plane invariant check that prevents rolebinding promotions during an active rotation window for tenants with critical compliance flags.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Stronger coordination increases rotation latency by up to 200–400ms in worst-case runs; acceptable under SLA for private customers but needs to be opt-in for Hosted.
- Persisting unwrap events for replay increases storage and S3 usage for private on-prem customers; we will cap retention to 48 hours and stream to existing audit logs to avoid duplication.

Rollout and verification plan:
- Stage rollout to private clusters: 1) internal staging (done), 2) non-production customer clusters, 3) high-trust customers (Finora Bank, Acme Analytics) with a canary period of 72 hours, 4) full private fleet.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1876 (rbac-index-coordination)
- Hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1882 (rotation-serialize-hotpatch)
- Post-deploy checks: monitor dashboard https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/org/private-rotation-safety and run the synthetic test harness for 10k simulated rotations/day.

Postmortem actions:
- Prepare a customer-facing incident summary and notify affected customers with mitigation steps and timelines.
- Expand e2e test coverage to include cross-component rotation+rbac scenarios in CI.
- Audit KMS-proxy retention and rekeying docs and update runbooks for on-call.

Notes: This ticket coordinates work across serving runtime, identity, and infra teams. Security review has been requested and scheduled for 2026-03-13.
